correctness.rationale: For each cube dimension, the contact criterion is proved equivalent to primitive three-periodicity by connectedness and forced color rotation. The exact single and pair defect probabilities follow from conditioning on center colors and shared neighbor counts. The variance, dependency b1/b2/b3, and coupling bound all follow algebraically with the exact 2-to-1 total-variation normalization in Arratia–Goldstein–Gordon (1989) Theorems 1 and 3. Disjoint-neighborhood packing supplies an independent global rarity bound. A standalone exhaustive program verifies direct dynamics and rational moment/pair calculations for d=1,2,3 and is supplied with matching captured output. Limit: finite check does not constitute infinite proof.

value.rationale: This is a natural high-dimensional initial-wave question in the canonical finite Greenberg–Hastings system. Exact opposite-sign local correlations coexist with asymptotic total-variation decoupling of all 2^d indicators; the number of defects explodes even though a fixed site almost surely has a viable excitation source, and disjoint-packing rigorously rules out typical immediate global waves. These facts offer a baseline for excitation coherence on high-dimensional networks, not a routine finite tabulation. The exact extreme no-defect asymptotic is deliberately not claimed.
